brief: September AI-related debt issuance fell to only ~$23bn globally, the second-lowest month this year. Morgan Stanley says the slowdown reflects front-loaded issuance earlier in the year, emerging regulatory and political constraints on data-center construction, and a rates selloff that may force project-level renegotiations, not weakening fundamentals or a shortage of capital, and expects a busier fall and fourth quarter as focus shifts to 2027 capex. In US investment grade, the bank views the macro backdrop, not supply, as the bigger test into year-end, expecting outflows given a 3% total-return drawdown on the year; its economists are more dovish than consensus, forecasting two more rate hikes versus the market's four, and expect high-quality hyperscalers to stay insensitive to higher rates given strong returns on invested capital. Year-to-date AI-related issuance totals $466bn versus $216bn in all of FY25. The bank prefers collateral-backed debt and colocation data-center ABS over hyperscaler shelves, and calls buying hyperscaler CDS protection its preferred way to play the AI story. ORCL issued a force majeure notice to Project Jupiter's developer, which Oracle said remains on schedule, while NVDA disclosed plans to reassign ~$20bn of future shell leases.
